entities.name: Thomas Tredwell
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Thomas Tredwell (1743–1831) was an American Anti-Federalist politician from New York who served in the Continental Congress (1787) and opposed ratification of the Constitution at the New York ratification convention (1788). Tredwell was one of the most articulate Anti-Federalist voices at New York's convention — a state where the battle over ratification was fierce and where the Anti-Federalist cause, led by Governor George Clinton, was very strong. His speech at the convention against the Constitution argued that it gave too much power to the federal government at the expense of state sovereignty and individual rights.

He later served in the New York State Legislature and held various state offices. Despite his constitutional opposition, he accepted the Constitution once ratified.

He was a Long Island New York farmer-lawyer and Anti-Federalist.

He was one of New York's most articulate voices against ratification.
